1.title: From Aperitif to Dessert: The Banquet Logic of Every Wine
1.html:
The rich and varied nature of Alsace varieties lets them accompany every dish from start to finish in a complete banquet — a quality of Alsace especially praised by France's "Best Sommelier" (Meilleur Sommelier du Monde 1989), Serge Dubs:

  • Aperitif (Apéritif): Crémant d'Alsace, Muscat d'Alsace, Gewurztraminer
  • Cold starters: salads / cold meats / oysters and seafood / sashimi and sushi → Sylvaner, Pinot Blanc, Riesling; spicy salads (Mexican / Moroccan / Indian flavours) → Gewurztraminer; foie gras → Pinot Gris or Gewurztraminer (the VT version is the most classic)
  • Hot starters: quiches, pies, soufflés → Sylvaner, Pinot Blanc; snails → Sylvaner; asparagus → Muscat d'Alsace, Pinot Blanc
2.title: Main Courses: Fish, White Meat, Red Meat and Game
2.html:
• Fish: pan-seared / grilled → Riesling; creamy white-sauce dishes → Riesling, Riesling VT, Pinot Gris; rich / spicy dishes → Pinot Gris, Gewurztraminer
  • White meat and poultry: roast poultry → Riesling, Pinot Blanc, Pinot Noir; poultry in sauce → Riesling, Pinot Gris; roast pork / veal → Pinot Blanc, Pinot Gris; duck → Pinot Gris; exotic dishes (sweet-and-savoury, heavily spiced) → Gewurztraminer
  • Red meat: mainly red-vinified Pinot Noir
  • Game: Pinot Gris or Pinot Noir depending on the cooking method
3.title: Choucroute, Cheese and Dessert: Alsace's Signature Finish
3.html:
Choucroute (Alsatian sauerkraut with meats) is the most representative home dish of the region — fermented sauerkraut stewed with sausages and smoked meats, classically paired with the fresh high acidity of Riesling or the refreshing sparkle of Crémant d'Alsace.

Cheese: fresh young cheeses and goat's cheese → Pinot Blanc, Riesling; soft washed-rind cheeses (Munster, Pont l'Évêque, blue cheese) → the rich aromas of Gewurztraminer neatly balance the strong smell; other cheeses also suit red-vinified Pinot Noir.

Dessert: pastries, tarts, cream sauces, mousses → Gewurztraminer (including the VT version); to put a perfect full stop to the whole meal, VT or SGN comes first; for social occasions or non-meal moments, Crémant, Muscat, Gewurztraminer, VT and SGN all suit.
4.title: Serving Temperature and Ageing Notes
4.html:
• Serving temperature: 8–10°C is recommended for AOC Alsace and Alsace Grand Cru; 5–7°C for Crémant d'Alsace — chilled but not iced, since over-cold wine masks the layers of aroma
  • Glassware: still Alsace wines suit a long-stemmed tulip-shaped glass; Crémant d'Alsace suits a slender crystal flute, and the glass should not be filled to the top, to let the aromas release fully
  • Drinking window: ordinary Alsace wines need no long ageing and show their rich flavours within six months to five years; but top vintages, Grand Cru, VT and SGN deserve longer ageing, stored in a cellar that is neither too dry nor too damp
  • Storage position: always lying flat, at an ambient temperature of 10–15°C; the tartrate crystals occasionally seen at the bottom of a bottle are natural, and often a sign of delicate wine quality
5.question: What is the most classic wine pairing for Alsace's classic home dish choucroute (sauerkraut with meats)?
5.options.1: The fresh high acidity of Riesling, or the refreshing sparkle of Crémant d'Alsace
5.explanation: Choucroute (Alsatian sauerkraut with meats) is made of fermented sauerkraut stewed with sausages and smoked meats; this sour and salty dish is best balanced by the fresh high acidity of Riesling, or contrasted refreshingly with the sparkle of Crémant d'Alsace, one of the most classic combinations in Alsace food pairing.
6.message: The complete picture of Alsace cuisine and food pairing complete!
6.keyPoints.0: Aperitif: Crémant, Muscat, Gewurztraminer; foie gras: Pinot Gris or Gewurztraminer (VT especially good)
6.keyPoints.1: Riesling first for fish; Riesling / Pinot Blanc / Pinot Noir for poultry; Gewurztraminer for exotic spicy dishes
6.keyPoints.2: Choucroute classically with Riesling or Crémant; strong cheeses such as Munster with Gewurztraminer
6.keyPoints.3: Serving temperature: AOC Alsace / Grand Cru 8–10°C, Crémant 5–7°C; drinking window six months to five years for ordinary wines, stored flat at 10–15°C
